newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh's Grameen Bank promotes small loans.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh's Grameen Bank promotes small loans.

text.p: Mohammad Yunus, chief executive of Bangladesh's Grameen Bank, said small loans offered by his bank had benefited 10 million rural poor people.
He also said the Grameen Bank had achieved a loan recovery record at 94 percent, much higher than commercial lending outlets.

At a meeting with chief executives of local banks and financial institutions in Dhaka on Wednesday, Yunus said one third of the Grameen Bank's 2.1 million borrowers had lifted themselves above the poverty line through self-employment.
"Another one-third was on the crossing point of the poverty line," he said, quoting a World Bank study, without elaborating.
Grameen Bank offers small income-generating loans without collateral to the extreme poor in rural areas
More than 90 percent of Grameen borrowers are women.
Yunus said his bank was operating in 36,000 of Bangladesh's 68,000 villages.
Almost half of Bangladesh's 120 million people live below the poverty line and about 68 percent are illiterate.
"We concentrate on rural areas so that people do not have to migrate to urban areas," Yunus said.
Started in 1976, the bank has lent about $400 million, with the average loan to individuals being $150.
Yunus said 52 countries, including China, had used the Grameen Bank's micro-credit model in fighting poverty and unemployment.
"Even the World Bank has now shrugged off its earlier suspicion about the success of micro-credit," Yunus said.
